$$

Which of the following is the image of the triangle shown above under the action of $T?$

examples.knowledge_point: Determining the Image of an Object Formed by a Singular Transformation
examples.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $\mathbf T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

  Find the image of the triangle shown below under the action of $\mathbf T.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13993138/assets/853fd7d5c09944a5bacd0c2b3453504f3fa1eea9d8d3b2c3bdd4f0f44889dc16.png)
examples.worked_solution:
To find the image of the triangle under the action of $\mathbf T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of the triangle:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $\mathbf T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -6 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the image's vertices are $(3,-6), (1,-2),$ and $(-2,4).$  Notice that all three points lie on the same line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13993138/assets/3fd1073b2eaa5aa9c21e537fcc4dc6cf538ab2992c0732f64da50dbcb63d8fd4.png)

feedback.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(0,2)$, $(-1,1)$ and $(3,1).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the action of $T?$

- $(12,6)$
- $(4,2)$
- $(4,6)$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the image of $S$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}12 & 4 & 12 \\ 6 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(12,6)$, $(4,2)$ and $(12,6).$

So, the correct answer is "I and II only."
